disease_label_per_paper: Acute rheumatic fever presenting with syncope due to complete atrioventricular block
presentation_summary: 15-year-old male was admitted to the emergency department because of syncope with closed consciousness and severe bradycardia.
He had joint pain in the preceding days and a history of tonsillopharyngitis 3 weeks before presentation.
Initial exam showed heart rate 33/min, temperature 37.2 C, respiratory rate 20/min, blood pressure 105/60 mmHg, and a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur.

ECG at presentation showed complete atrioventricular block with ventricular rate 33/min. Echocardiography, ASO, Jones adjudication, and treatment response are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context unless explicitly tested in a post-workup mode.
Laboratory testing showed WBC 13,470/mm3, ESR 26 mm/h, CRP 37 mg/L, normal troponin T and CK-MB, and elevated ASO 1270 IU/mL.

observations.source_text_value: admitted to the emergency department because of syncope
had joint pain in the last days
complete AVB was observed in ECG
symptomatic complete AVB requiring transient pacemaker electrode
systolic ejection murmur plus complete AV block during suspected rheumatic carditis
Troponin T levels were found to be normal

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: A diagnosis of ARA was made with carditis as one major finding and increased acute phase reactants and arthralgia as two minor findings with supportive increased ASO

actual_treatment: transient pacemaker electrode placed in the right ventricle
oral methylprednisolone 16 mg three times daily
benzathine penicillin G 1,200,000 IU intramuscular with 21-day prophylaxis recommendation
acetylsalicylic acid started in the second week

outcome.clinical_course: Complete AV block improved to first-degree AV block on the third day of steroid treatment, temporary pacing was terminated, acute phase reactants normalized on day 4, and first-degree AV block recovered by week 3.
outcome.source_text_value: On the third day ... first-degree AVB ... transient pacemaker treatment was terminated ... in the third week ... first-degree AVB was also recovered

quality_warnings: ASO, echocardiographic valve regurgitation, and paper Jones adjudication are confirmatory_findings with use_in_ranking:false.
Normal troponin T is preserved but not ranked because the paper gives no numeric value; encoding a qualitative normal result as 0 ng/L creates an artificial residual.
The rankable presentation keeps the critical clinical evidence: syncope, complete AV block, severe bradycardia, recent tonsillopharyngitis, arthralgia, murmur, and inflammatory markers.
